headline: Solaris identified Suncorp as a contrarian buy in 2022, capitalising on improving insurance industry structure as La Nina-driven catastrophes abated and competitive tension eased.

The team anticipated that a shift from La Nina to El Nino would reduce catastrophe frequency, allowing Suncorp to raise prices. The stock subsequently re-rated from 11x to 16x P/E as profits materially increased.
quote: What we saw in the case of Suncorp, we saw a company that had been sold right off. It was trading on a P of 10 or 11 times. It was at cyclical low earnings. What really hit home to us in terms of that industry structure was we do a lot of meetings, as you talked about before, Rian, and we see a lot of unlisted companies. We visit a lot of the unlisted insurers, so the budgets, the UEs of the world really to get an idea of the competitive landscape. Prior to those catastrophes, you saw those companies competing really hard with the likes of IAG and Suncorp. IAG and Suncorp were losing a lot of market share. That was our industry structure that was deteriorating. When we saw those catastrophes happen, what you saw was a lot of those brands like the budgets and the UEs really pulled back their competitive tension because a lot of capital had been lost throughout those catastrophes.
